description:
CSUTLDTC, the called date-validation subprogram, invoked as the @Service it became (util.DateUtilityJob) and never through a JobLauncher or an HTTP layer: no EXEC PGM= anywhere in app/jcl or app/proc names it, and it is CALLed four times from two online programs - CORPT00C at L392 and L412, COTRN02C at L393 and L413. LS-DATE='          ' and LS-DATE-FORMAT='YYYY-MM-DD' are this case's two LINKAGE SECTION parameters (L84-L85), each written out to the declared PIC X(10) width; the date is ten blanks, which is the whole point of the case. LS-RESULT PIC X(80) (L86) is the entire output and is asserted below as the single WS_MESSAGE_80 line. The program declares no ENVIRONMENT DIVISION, no SELECT and no FD, so it seeds no dataset, writes no record and leaves no final state to state; it also declares no job parameter, and not merely because no JCL reaches it - ParityCase refuses a job parameter on any unitKind but BATCH_JOB, since an input member holding a value the case also expects would be fed back into the unit and then compared against itself. Its entire observable behaviour is the 80 bytes L97 moves into LS-RESULT and the severity L98 moves into RETURN-CODE. This case pins arm 8 of the ten-arm EVALUATE TRUE at L128-L149: FC-NON-NUMERIC-DATA, 88-level VALUE X'000309D859C3C5C5' (L69). Both numbers in the message are DECODED from that hex rather than interpolated from the neighbouring arms - the leading halfword 0x0003 is the severity, which L123 renders '0003' through the WS-SEVERITY-N PIC 9(4) REDEFINES at L44 and L98 moves to RETURN-CODE as 3, and the second halfword 0x09D8 is message 2520, which L124 renders '2520' through the WS-MSG-NO-N REDEFINES at L47. The trailing 59 C3 C5 C5 is the condition's severity-control byte and its facility identifier, and those last three bytes spell 'CEE' only when read as EBCDIC, never as ASCII; they take no part in the message. Arm 8 is reached here by a quite different route from case18's, and the route is the reason this case exists: case18 stands a letter in every numeric position, whereas here the mask is the well-formed one from case01 and the date supplies no character at all. What that pins is a precedence in an ordered guard chain where the first failure wins. The picture string parses, so this is not 2518; it carries a year, a month and a day, so it is not 2507 either, and 2507 is in any case attributed to the picture string rather than to a deficient input date; the failure is therefore taken at the shape check, where a numeric position that supplies no digit at all is 2520, the code IBM documents for non-numeric data found where numeric data was expected. That distinction is easy to get wrong, because blank tolerance is genuine: leading and trailing blanks around a numeric field ARE accepted, so a validator could plausibly have read an all-blank date as an omitted value and defaulted it, or have blamed the mask instead. It does neither, and this case is what holds it to that. WS-DATE at offset 45 then reports eight blanks behind two binary bytes, which is worth pinning on a blank input precisely because nothing else in the line moves: L105-L106 takes LENGTH OF LS-DATE - the DECLARED length, hence always 10 - into VSTRING-LENGTH, and the GROUP move at L122 overwrites the clean copy made at L107-L108 with the leftmost ten bytes of WS-DATE-TO-TEST, which are the Vstring-length halfword X'000A' followed by only the first eight characters. That corruption is expected output and is preserved rather than corrected. WS-DATE-FMT at offset 66 is by contrast clean, because L111-L113 set it by an ordinary X(10) to X(10) move before the CALL and L122 targets WS-DATE alone. The line is eighty bytes wide whatever the input was, and the 01 WS-MESSAGE declaration at L42-L57 is summed span by span to prove it: 4 + 11 + 4 + 1 + 15 + 1 + 9 + 10 + 1 + 10 + 10 + 1 + 3 = 80, with 'Mesg Code:' ten characters inside a PIC X(11) span and 'TstDate:' eight inside a PIC X(09), each right-padded by its own VALUE clause, while 'Mask used:' exactly fills its PIC X(10) and needs no pad; INITIALIZE at L90 does not clear a FILLER, so all three literals survive. On the tenth arm, for the record, because this file sits beside it: WHEN OTHER at L147-L148 moves 'Date is invalid' - already exactly fifteen characters, and not to be confused with arm 1's 'Date is valid', which is thirteen plus two of pad and carries the opposite meaning - and it must remain last, since EVALUATE takes the first matching WHEN and this arm is the default. It has no 88-level VALUE of its own, and no input date can select it. The nine enumerated message numbers are 0 for the all-zeros success token at L62 and then 2507, 2508, 2509, 2513, 2517, 2518, 2520 and 2521, a non-contiguous set whose gaps are 2510, 2511, 2512, 2514, 2515, 2516 and 2519; so a structurally genuine feedback token such as X'000309D759C3C5C5' - severity 0x0003, message 0x09D7 = 2519 sitting squarely in that gap, the same 0x59 control byte and the same EBCDIC 'CEE' facility every named error token carries - matches none of the nine 88 levels at L62-L70 and would necessarily fall through to arm 10. Such a token is what a real Language Environment might return and what this translation never manufactures, which is why arm 10 is exercised where its mapping actually lives - by DateUtilityJobTest through the package-private resultTextOfFeedbackToken seam in com.vsergeychik.carddemo.util - rather than from a parity case, which would have to carry the token in as an input and then assert its own decode straight back out. Expected values here are STATICALLY DERIVED by structured reading of app/cbl/CSUTLDTC.cbl - the WS-MESSAGE spans at L42-L57, the nine tokens at L62-L70, the arm literal at L144, the group move at L122 and the EVALUATE at L128-L149 - and were NOT captured from any execution of the COBOL, which is impossible in this environment: PROCEDURE DIVISION USING at L88 makes this a subprogram the available compiler refuses to build as an executable, and cobc --list-intrinsics matches zero CEE* entries, so the CALL "CEEDAYS" at L116 that decides every outcome has no implementation to call. Only the provenance of the expectation is substituted; the twenty-case set, the field-by-field diff and the diff-count-of-zero gate all stand.

THE TWO CALL PARAMETERS, DECLARED RATHER THAN SELECTED IN JAVA. unitStimulus.linkage carries this case's whole input: LS-DATE = '          ' and LS-DATE-FORMAT = 'YYYY-MM-DD', each written out to the ten characters PIC X(10) declares at app/cbl/CSUTLDTC.cbl:84-85 with every trailing space visible - a mask longer than ten characters is TRUNCATED by the receiving field, and the truncation changes the message number, so the width has to be readable at the point the value is written. CSUTLDTC seeds no dataset and drives no screen, so these two values are the only thing a case varies; they used to live in a table in CSUTLDTCParityTest keyed by 'case01'..'case20', which meant this file stated an eighty-byte result with nothing in it to say what was validated, and cases that differ only in their input were indistinguishable on disk.
